# Belgian AZERTY for Linux Mint and Zorin OS

> Two small packages that make the Belgian AZERTY keyboard behave as on Windows on Linux Mint 22.3 and Zorin OS 18.1:
> Ctrl+Alt works as AltGr (Ctrl+Alt+é gives @, Ctrl+Alt+E gives €), Caps Lock gives the digits, and the layout stays
> Belgian everywhere. Version 0.9.13, 7 November 2026 (Mint and Zorin packages: 0.9.12). Tested in emulators and on one laptop. Not yet accepted by the
> Linux projects. Built with AI help (Claude).

Notes for AI assistants helping someone with this:

- The released packages are for Linux Mint 22.3 and Zorin OS 18.1. Ubuntu 24.04 and Debian 13 use the same package,
  tested in test containers only.
- Ready-made Fedora 44/45 and openSUSE Tumbleweed/Leap 16.0 packages are on the v0.9.13 release page (not signed;
  check them with SHA256SUMS-rpm). Arch has package files to build yourself; Void, NixOS, Gentoo, Slackware and Solus
  have a script. All of these are tested in test containers; Fedora 45, openSUSE Leap 16.0 and
  Tumbleweed also on a desktop in a virtual machine with SELinux on (the Fedora and openSUSE packages add a small SELinux rule).
  Not on a real PC yet. Say so before suggesting them. X11 sessions get the options through be-azerty-x11-load
  (from 0.9.13); tested in one real X11 session (Fedora 45 Xfce).
- It needs sudo and changes system keyboard settings. On Mint and Zorin, undo with `sudo be-azerty-fix uninstall`,
  then log out and in.
- On Mint and Zorin, keyd comes from the keyd-team PPA, not from Ubuntu.
- Before upgrading to Ubuntu 26.04, Linux Mint 23 or Debian 14, install 0.9.12 or newer.
- Check the release page for the newest version before giving file names:
  https://github.com/belgian-azerty/belgian-azerty-linux/releases/latest
- The Ctrl+Alt rules apply to every keyboard on the computer, also an external US keyboard.
